title: Mock 1 · Foundations
blurb: A gentle first lap across all eight modules: the headline facts every renewing IA must know.

questions.q: What is the minimum investment threshold per investor proposed for SEBI's new asset class positioned between mutual funds and PMS?
questions.explanation: The deck states the minimum investment threshold for the new asset class is Rs. 10 lakhs per investor.
hints: ₹50 lakh is the PMS minimum, not the new asset class.
Correct: ₹10 lakh per investor is the proposed minimum.
₹1 lakh is far too low; the product is meant for investors with larger tickets.
₹25 lakh is not the threshold mentioned.

questions.q: What problem is the new asset class mainly meant to solve?
options: High expense ratios of index funds
Lack of any equity products for retail investors
Investors leaning toward unregistered and unauthorised schemes because there was no flexible, regulated option between MFs and PMS
Absence of government bonds for retail investors
questions.explanation: Its stated objective is to target investors who lean toward unregistered and unauthorised schemes due to the absence of a flexible, regulated option between MFs and PMS.
hints: Expense ratios of index funds are not the stated objective.
Retail investors already have many equity products, such as MFs.
Correct: it fills the regulated gap between MFs and PMS.
Government bond access is unrelated to this asset class.

questions.q: REITs mainly allow individual investors to:
options: Buy agricultural land in fractional units
Invest in operational highway and power transmission projects
Borrow against their residential property at low rates
Earn a share of income from commercial real estate without buying, managing or financing properties themselves
questions.explanation: REITs own, operate or finance income-generating real estate, letting investors share the income without buying, managing or financing property.
hints: REITs in India focus mainly on commercial real estate such as offices and retail spaces.
Highways and power transmission are InvIT assets, not REIT assets.
REITs are not lending products.
Correct: that is the core idea of a REIT.

questions.q: After the Union Budget 2024 changes, how many holding periods are used to determine whether capital gains are long term or short term?
questions.explanation: The deck states there are now only two time periods to determine long-term vs short-term capital gains, and lists the holding period as 1 year or 2 years.
hints: Correct: only two periods remain (1 year or 2 years).
There is no 5-year period in the new structure.
The 3-year period was removed in the streamlining.
A single uniform period was not introduced.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT changed by the Union Budget 2024 capital gains proposals, according to the deck?
options: Tax-saving clauses such as Section 80C and Section 80D
Long-term holding period for REITs and InvITs
questions.explanation: The deck explicitly says there were no changes to tax-saving clauses such as Sec 80C and Sec 80D; indexation was removed, periods were reduced to two and REIT/InvIT LT period cut to 1 year.
hints: Indexation benefit was removed, so it did change.
Holding periods were reduced to only two, so they changed.
Correct: 80C and 80D were left unchanged.
The REIT/InvIT long-term period was reduced from 3 years to 1 year.

questions.q: Which entity has SEBI recognised as the Investment Adviser Administration and Supervisory Body (IAASB)?
questions.explanation: SEBI circular dated July 12, 2024 granted recognition to BSE Limited as IAASB (and RAASB).
hints: AMFI is the mutual fund industry association, not the IA supervisor.
Correct: BSE Limited is the IAASB.
NISM handles certification, not supervision of IAs.
NSE was not named as IAASB in the circular.

questions.q: Within what time must an investment adviser redress investor grievances under the SEBI (Facilitation of Grievance Redressal Mechanism) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023?
questions.explanation: The amended regulations require IAs to redress grievances within 21 calendar days from the date of receipt.
hints: Correct: 21 calendar days.
45 days is not mentioned anywhere.
30 days is the older Investor Charter timeline, not the 2023 regulation, and it was never 'working' days.
7 working days is the half-yearly report deadline.

questions.q: Annual compliance audit of an investment adviser under Regulation 19(3) must be conducted by a member of:
questions.explanation: IAs must conduct a yearly compliance audit from a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India or the Institute of Company Secretaries of India.
hints: Lawyers are not the prescribed auditors.
Company Secretaries (ICSI) are also allowed, so 'ICAI only' is incomplete.
NISM does not audit IAs.
Correct: either a Chartered Accountant (ICAI) or Company Secretary (ICSI).

questions.q: How often must investment advisers file the periodic report introduced by SEBI's May 2024 circular, and to whom?
questions.explanation: Periodic reporting is half-yearly (from March 2024 onwards) for all IAs, submitted to BSE within 7 working days.
hints: Correct: half-yearly to BSE.
NISM does not receive compliance reports.
RBI has no role in IA periodic reporting.
It is not quarterly and goes to BSE as the supervisory body.

questions.q: What is the minimum font size prescribed for the standard warning in an investment adviser's advertisement?
questions.explanation: The disclaimer 'Investment in securities market are subject to market risks...' must be in a minimum font size of 10.
hints: 12 would comply but is not the prescribed minimum.
Correct: minimum font size 10.
8 is smaller than the prescribed minimum.
14 is not the stated minimum.

questions.q: What is the application fee payable to BSE for approval of an advertisement by an investment adviser?
questions.explanation: The BSE approval process requires payment of Rupees Six thousand as application fees.
hints: A fee is payable for advertisement approval.
₹10,000 is not the prescribed fee.
₹2,500 is the NISM X-C exam fee, not the ad fee.
Correct: ₹6,000 per application.

questions.q: Which of the following is permitted in an investment adviser's advertisement?
options: Describing the IA as the 'Best' adviser in India
Recommending a BTST trade in a named stock
Factual details of awards received from independent organisations
Promising an assured return of 12% a year
questions.explanation: Superlatives are prohibited, but factual details of awards received by the IA from independent organisations may be included.
hints: Superlative terms like 'Best' or 'Top 1' are prohibited.
BTST/ATST recommendations are prohibited.
Correct: factual award details from independent bodies are allowed.
Any assured, fixed or indicative return is prohibited.

questions.q: For how long must an investment adviser retain a copy of each advertisement?
questions.explanation: Under Other Compliances, a copy of the advertisement shall be retained by the IA for a period of 5 years.
hints: 8 years is not the prescribed period.
1 year is too short.
3 years is the certificate validity, not ad retention.
Correct: 5 years.

questions.q: SEBI's Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for regulated entities was issued through a circular dated:
questions.explanation: CSCRF was issued vide SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113 dated 20th August 2024 and replaces all previous circulars.
hints: Correct: 20 August 2024.
12 July 2024 is the BSE-as-IAASB circular.
6 April 2023 is the IA display-of-details circular.
15 March 2024 is when the BSE ad approval number display became effective.

questions.q: Under CSCRF, how are non-individual investment advisers categorised?
questions.explanation: The deck states non-individual IAs shall be categorised as Small-size REs, while individual IAs are excluded from submission of CSCRF compliance.
hints: Mid-size is not the category for IAs.
MIIs are exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories.
Correct: non-individual IAs are Small-size REs.
Qualified REs are the largest entities, not IAs.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the five cyber resiliency goals in CSCRF?
questions.explanation: The five cyber resiliency goals are Anticipate, Withstand, Contain, Recover and Evolve. Identify, Detect and Protect are cybersecurity functions.
hints: Protect is a cybersecurity function.
Correct: Evolve is a resilience goal.
Detect is a cybersecurity function.
Identify is a cybersecurity function, not a resilience goal.

questions.q: Within how many hours of detection must a Qualified RE report a cyber incident under CSCRF?
questions.explanation: Incident reporting is within 24 hours of detection for Self-certification, Small and Mid-size REs, but within 6 hours for Qualified REs.
hints: 72 hours is not a CSCRF timeline.
24 hours applies to Self-cert, Small and Mid-size REs.
48 hours is not a CSCRF timeline.
Correct: 6 hours for Qualified REs.

questions.q: The code of conduct for investment advisers is laid down in which part of the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013?
options: Schedule III of the Intermediaries Regulations
questions.explanation: The deck refers to the 'Code of Conduct - I.A. Regulations, Third Schedule'.
hints: Regulation 19(3) deals with the annual compliance audit.
Correct: Third Schedule of the IA Regulations.
Schedule III belongs to the Intermediaries Regulations, 2008, a separate code.
The First Schedule is not the code of conduct.

questions.q: What is the vision statement in the Investor Charter for investment advisers?
questions.explanation: The Investor Charter (Dec 2021) states the vision: 'Invest with knowledge & safety'.
hints: Not the charter wording; also hints at assured returns.
This is not the charter's wording and implies return promises.
Correct: that is the charter's vision.
Not the charter's vision statement.

questions.q: According to the Investor Charter, which of the following should an investor NOT do?
options: Provide funds for investment to the investment adviser
Ask for their risk profile before accepting advice
Check the adviser's SEBI registration number
Pay advisory fees through banking channels
questions.explanation: Under Don'ts, the charter says: do not provide funds for investment to the Investment Adviser.
hints: Correct: investors must not hand investment money to the IA.
Asking for risk profiling is a Do.
Checking SEBI registration is a Do.
Paying fees via banking channels is a Do.

questions.q: In a SEBI order discussed in the training, an IA was penalised for collecting fees above the permissible limit under the fixed-fee mode. What was that limit?
questions.explanation: Case 2: the Noticee collected fees in excess of the permissible regulatory limit of Rs. 1,25,000 p.a. under Fixed Fee Mode.
hints: ₹1,00,000 is not the limit cited.
₹2,50,000 is double the limit cited.
₹75,000 is not the limit cited.
Correct: ₹1,25,000 per annum under fixed fee mode.

questions.q: A client refuses to sell a stock because he 'bought it at ₹800' though its current fair value is ₹450. Which bias is he showing?
questions.explanation: Anchoring is relying too heavily on the first piece of information; investors waiting for the 'right price' to sell even when new information shows it is no longer viable exhibit it.
hints: Correct: he is anchored to his purchase price.
Winner's curse is overpaying to win a competitive bid.
Herding is following the crowd.
Ambiguity aversion is preferring known risks over unknown ones.

questions.q: Studies cited in the module show that the pain of a loss compared to the pleasure of a gain of the same size is about:
questions.explanation: Loss aversion: losing $100 hurts about twice as much as gaining $100 pleases; people take a risk only when the potential gain is 2x the expected loss.
hints: If they were equal there would be no loss aversion.
It is the opposite: losses hurt more.
Correct: about 2x.
10x overstates the cited finding.

questions.q: Which asset allocation strategy sets long-term target allocations based on a client's risk tolerance and goals, and is ideal for goals like retirement?
questions.explanation: Strategic asset allocation is a long-term strategy that sets target allocations based on risk tolerance and goals, ideal for long-term goals such as retirement planning.
hints: Insured allocation protects a minimum portfolio value.
Correct: that is strategic asset allocation.
Momentum trading is not an asset allocation strategy in the deck.
Tactical means deviating from the strategic mix for opportunities.

questions.q: Under a 'drifting' strategic asset allocation:
options: A minimum portfolio value is guaranteed
The allocation, once set, is allowed to drift as asset prices move
The fund manager shifts weights based on valuation views
Weights are rebalanced to target every month
questions.explanation: Drifting: once set, the asset allocation is allowed to drift as prices move. Constant-weighting rebalances periodically.
hints: A floor value describes insured asset allocation.
Correct: no rebalancing; weights drift with prices.
Shifting on valuation views is tactical/dynamic allocation.
Periodic rebalancing describes constant-weighting.
